questions.q: What is a Terraform module, structurally?
options: A directory of .tf files — the same thing you've been writing as the root module all along
A compiled binary plugin separate from provider plugins
A single resource block tagged with a special module attribute
A JSON file that cannot contain resource blocks
questions.explain: A module is just a folder of .tf files. The directory you run terraform apply from is itself called the root module.

questions.q: Why did Northbridge Retail move its storage account resource block into a module instead of leaving it in the root configuration?
options: Because resource blocks are not allowed to repeat across environments
Because dev, staging, and production all need the same resource pattern, and copy-pasting it three times means three places to fix the same bug
Because modules run faster than resource blocks
Because Azure requires modules for storage accounts specifically
questions.explain: A module exists to avoid maintaining duplicate copies of the same resource pattern across environments.

questions.q: Which argument is required on every module block?
options: version
source
provider
backend
questions.explain: source tells Terraform where the module's files live, whether a local path or a registry address.

questions.q: If a root configuration calls the same child module twice — once as module "storage_dev" and once as module "storage_staging" — how does Terraform treat the two calls?
options: As a single shared resource that gets overwritten by whichever call runs last
As an error, since a module can only be called once per configuration
As two completely separate instances, each with its own address in state
As identical resources that must have identical input values
questions.explain: Each module block is its own instance; Terraform namespaces resources under each call separately, e.g. module.storage_dev.azurerm_storage_account.this.

questions.q: What command must you run after adding a new module block, before terraform plan will work?
options: terraform init, so Terraform can resolve and install the module's source
terraform destroy, to clear out the old configuration
terraform fmt, to reformat the module's files
No command is needed — plan always resolves modules automatically
questions.explain: terraform init resolves and installs a module's source the same way it installs provider plugins.
